items.title: Salts of strong acids and strong bases (printed as a second 9.8.1)

source_refs.note: Salts of Strong Acids and Strong Bases, printed as a second 9.8.1 on page 204.

blocks.text: For salts derived from strong acids and strong bases, such as sodium chloride, the conjugate base of the strong acid (Cl- from HCl) is very weak and does not react significantly with water, and the conjugate acid of the strong base (Na+ from NaOH) is also very weak and does not react significantly with water. NaCl(s) in water gives Na+(aq) + Cl-(aq): Na+ is the conjugate acid of the strong base NaOH and does not affect the pH; Cl- is the conjugate base of the strong acid HCl and does not affect the pH. The solution remains neutral.
